findings.reason: the repair must also stop the command naming a text review and must obtain the figure review run id, neither of which §24 mentions, so a node following it would add `--rubric figure` to a command that still names the text round and ship a command that fails differently from the one described.
findings.text: §24's Why says the suggested command "fails with 'carries no record' because a figure record is selected only with `--rubric figure`", but `dispose_commands` (reckon/crew/review_dispositions.py:506-525) is never given `review_run_id` by any production caller — its only callers are `_finding_dispose_commands` (reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:2458-2471) and the dimension loop (reckon/crew/obligations.py:2510), and none passes it — so it falls back to `_newest_delivered_review_run_id`, which calls `newest_delivered_review(..., rubric=None)`, where `_review_rubric_matches` excludes figure records (reckon/crew/review.py:2717-2718); the fallback there never names the figure review run. The real outcome is worse than the stated one: with a text review present the command names the text review and `crew dispose --finding N` writes the figure record's index onto the text record, and with no text review it raises "no stored review for run … to record a disposition against" (reckon/crew_run_commands.py:1049-1055).

findings.reason: without naming those call sites as write paths and stating that the composer must be handed the rubric and the figure review run, the node hits its write fence mid-implementation and either stops as blocked or widens scope unilaterally.
findings.text: §24's first measured case (a duty's dispose command includes `--rubric figure` and running it records the disposition) is not reachable from the section's write paths: `dispose_commands` alone cannot tell a figure duty from a text one, because its only knowledge of the record is `review_run_id`, which no caller passes; the rubric is in hand only at the loops that hold the record — `_finding_dispose_commands` (reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:2458-2471) and reckon/crew/obligations.py:706,809 — while the write paths are `reckon/crew/review_dispositions.py` and the new test. Passing `--rubric figure` beside the fallback's text `--review` makes the command fail "carries no record from review run <text>" (reckon/crew_run_commands.py:930-935), so the case cannot pass without editing files the section does not grant.

findings.reason: a worker taking "sub-floor" literally inspects the dimension path, finds no figure duty raised there, and can conclude the defect does not reproduce or that the fix belongs in `_sub_floor_items_by_session`, where it would change nothing for a figure review.
findings.text: §24 calls the defect "a sub-floor figure-review finding", which names the wrong duty path: a figure review scores no dimensions (reckon/crew_run_commands.py:898-903 refuses `--dimension` on a figure record, and `_sub_floor_items_by_session` reads only the text record through `stored_review_for_run`, reckon/crew/obligations.py:2478-2513), so the duty a figure finding actually raises is the blocking-finding review refusal (`_open_review_refusal` → `_undisposed_blocking_findings`, reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:2489-2545).

findings.reason: the followup is how the plan closes its chain visibly; without one naming §24, the recommended invocation points at a section that cannot run while the runnable one is invisible to a coordinator reading the followups.
findings.text: §24 was added as `implementable` but the plan's only open followup, `f-arcstf-009`, still recommends `/reckon-build a-review-can-see-the-figure §20` (held on `imas-ambix:a-tool-call-carries-no-model-markup#s3`), and no followup names §24, so the plan hands a coordinator no one-line invocation for the section it just made dispatchable.
